s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disease with autoimmune features, characterized by skin, joint, and lung involvement, with a prolonged course of symptoms and significant weight loss
salient_findings: Symmetric swelling of metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints with ulcers
Dyspigmentation and atrophy of distal fingers
Bibasilar rales and interstitial lung disease on chest CT
Elevated ferritin and lymphocytopenia
Positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies
key_facts: 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, tender ulcerations, hair loss, and weight loss
Previous hospitalization for hypoxia 6 months prior
Previous treatment with prednisone
Symmetric joint swelling preventing fist formation
Dorsal MCPs had ulcers, distal fingers were dyspigmented and atrophic
Normal capillaroscopy
Palmar IP creases had ulcerated lichenoid papules
Oxford Scale muscle strength was 5 of 5 throughout
Aldolase: 4.5 U/L (normal)
Creatine kinase: 32 U/L (depressed)
Ferritin: 1543 ng/mL (elevated)
Lymphocytopenia with CD3: 328 μL, CD4: 233 μL, CD8: 85 μL
Positive for anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies
Positive for immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies (19.5 units)
Chest CT showed hilar lymphadenopathy, interstitial thickening, and perilymphatic ground glass opacities
Pulmonary function tests showed restrictive disease with decreased diffusing capacity (33% predicted)

raw.syndrome_frame: Chronic multisystem disease with autoimmune features, characterized by skin, joint, and lung involvement, with a prolonged course of symptoms and significant weight loss

Dyspigmentation and atrophy of distal fingers
Bibasilar rales and interstitial lung disease on chest CT
Elevated ferritin and lymphocytopenia

key_facts: 7-month history of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, tender ulcerations, hair loss, and weight loss
Previous hospitalization for hypoxia 6 months prior
Previous treatment with prednisone
Symmetric joint swelling preventing fist formation
Dorsal MCPs had ulcers, distal fingers were dyspigmented and atrophic
Normal capillaroscopy
Palmar IP creases had ulcerated lichenoid papules
Oxford Scale muscle strength was 5 of 5 throughout
Aldolase: 4.5 U/L (normal)
Creatine kinase: 32 U/L (depressed)

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, arthralgias, hand swelling, tender ulcerations, hair loss, and weight loss, along with laboratory findings of elevated ferritin, lymphocytopenia, and positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, are consistent with Systemic Lupus Erythematosus. The presence of immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies also supports this diagnosis, as antiphospholipid syndrome is often seen in conjunction with SLE.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: While the patient has some features of MCTD, such as arthralgias and hand swelling, the presence of anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies and immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies points more towards SLE.

rejected.label: Antiphospholipid Syndrome
rejected.why: Although the patient has positive immunoglobulin G anticardiolipin antibodies, the clinical presentation and other laboratory findings are more consistent with SLE than primary antiphospholipid syndrome.

rejected.label: Scleroderma
rejected.why: The patient's skin biopsy showed orthokeratosis and diffuse vasculopathy, but lacked the characteristic sclerotic changes seen in scleroderma.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient has positive anti-SSA (Ro) antibodies, which are commonly seen in Sjögren's syndrome, the overall clinical presentation and laboratory findings are more consistent with SLE.
